written.myAnswer: A mole is an amount of substance containing Avogadro’s number of particles. Avogadro’s number is the numerical value 6.022 × 10²³ particles per mole.

Different compounds can have the same empirical formula (the same simplest whole-number ratio of atoms) but different molecular formulae, because their molecules can contain different numbers of those atoms.
Calcium phosphate: Ca₃(PO₄)₂; aluminium nitride: AlN; sodium acetate: CH₃COONa; ammonium carbonate: (NH₄)₂CO₃; bismuth sulphate: Bi₂(SO₄)₃.
Avogadro’s number relates the number of particles to the amount of substance in moles, allowing chemists to calculate particle quantities from measurable amounts such as mass.
